item.title: Phosphoric Acid Cross-linking Regulates Closed Pores for Scalable Hard Carbon Anodes
item.description:
استراتژی اتصال عرضی با اسید فسفریک، حفرات بسته کربن سخت مشتق از نشاسته را تنظیم کرده و ظرفیت ۳۹۵.۸ mAh g−1 در آند باتری سدیم-یون ایجاد می‌کند.
ACS Energy Letters | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This work introduces phosphoric acid-induced cross-linking as a novel strategy to precisely regulate closed pores in starch-derived hard carbon. It boosts carbon yield from 14.0% to 31.7% and delivers 395.8 mAh g⁻¹ with 89.4% initial Coulombic efficiency. The 3.5 Ah cylindrical cell retains 96.5% capacity after 500 cycles, offering a scalable, cost-effective route for practical Na-ion battery anodes.
🏷 hard carbon anode · sodium-ion battery · closed pores · phosphoric acid · cross-linking

item.description:

Advanced Functional Materials | ⭐ Review
💡 This Review reframes MOF-derived battery electrodes around how conversion rewrites precursor information into working structures and interfaces, distinguishing retention, reconstruction, erasure, and emergence. Its novelty lies in this material-centered, function-oriented framework linking precursor chemistry to interfacial continuity and reversible reaction, rather than cataloguing products. It matters because it guides predictive design, operando characterization, and practical deployment balancing performance against inactive mass, complexity, and cost.
🏷 MOF-derived electrodes · rechargeable batteries · precursor conversion · interfaces · structure reconstruction

item.title: From Brittle to Damage‐Tolerant: Particle‐Level Mechanical Reinforcement Enables High‐Voltage Stability in Ni‐Rich Cathodes
item.description:
تقویت مکانیکی در سطح ذره، کاتد غنی از نیکل را از ترد به مقاوم به آسیب تبدیل کرده و پایداری چرخه در ولتاژ بالا را به‌شدت بهبود می‌دهد.
Small | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This work pioneers particle-level mechanical reinforcement of Ni-rich cathodes, achieving a fivefold crushing-strength increase and reduced stress accumulation, which suppresses fracture during high-voltage cycling. The strategy enables 81% capacity retention over 400 cycles versus 36.5% undoped, establishing mechanics-informed design as a generalizable principle for damage-tolerant high-voltage cathodes.
